t.E302.agn: In 2015 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern at the reported use levels.
t.E302.body: In the body it breaks down into ascorbic acid (vitamin C) and calcium; excess vitamin C is excreted in the urine.
t.E302.prod: Obtained by reacting vitamin C (ascorbic acid) with calcium carbonate; ascorbic acid is produced from glucose by fermentation and chemical steps.
t.E302.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern.
t.E302.summary: The calcium salt of vitamin C. It is used as an antioxidant and as a source of vitamin.
t.E302.what: It is the calcium salt of vitamin C; by slowing oxidation it prevents deterioration of colour and flavour.
